title: DAYDRIFT podcast episode-art package: pull a frame from three mixed-lighting episodes, grade them to one channel look, vectorize the photographed logo, and data-merge one press-ready episode card per episode
grounding_note: Adapted from a real Freelancer.com YouTube-podcast brief (raw episode footage to be shaped into engaging episodes, 'weave in light-hearted graphics that match a casual, fun vibe', incorporate the client's existing logo across the channel branding, and deliver 'any custom graphic assets you create, delivered separately in PNG/transparent or vector format'). Two literal asks in that brief are NOT connector-doable and are honestly re-cast rather than faked: (1) a Premiere/FCP timeline trim of 'pauses and stumbles' has no connector analog (video_create_quick_cut is engagement-based, not timestamp trimming), and (2) compositing graphics INTO the video is out of scope and the brief itself asks for the graphic assets delivered SEPARATELY. So the job is repositioned to the channel-artwork package a podcast editor actually owes between episodes and that the connector genuinely produces: a tonally-matched episode-thumbnail set built from real frames pulled out of the raw episodes, a cleaned + vectorized channel logo, and a per-episode printable episode card produced by a one-file-per-row InDesign data-merge for the press/sponsor kit. The client brand is laundered to a fictional casual culture-and-chat YouTube podcast, 'DAYDRIFT' (navy + coral palette, small paper-boat/drift glyph); no real person, show, brand, or trademark is named. ENRICHMENT (to make the chain concrete, failable and measurable): the three episodes were recorded on different nights under different studio lighting so their frames do not match out of camera, and a neutral 18% grey reference card is clipped to the desk mic-flag in every episode so white balance can be reconciled after the fact; the frame-pull count, the per-episode casts, the neon-sign recolor, the crop dimensions, and the authored .indd + roster are reasonable enrichment consistent with the source.
one_line_ask: Pull a representative frame from each of three DAYDRIFT episodes shot under different studio lighting, neutralize each to the 18% grey card it carries so the thumbnail set reads as one channel look (deciding per frame how far to move white balance, and NOT 'correcting' the episode whose warmth is intentional), deepen the on-set coral neon sign to the true brand coral on the hero frame with a masked pass, clean and vectorize the photographed channel logo, then data-merge the client's authored single-record episode-card template against the roster to produce one press-ready card per episode plus the YouTube thumbnail set.
full_brief:
We run DAYDRIFT, a casual culture-and-chat YouTube podcast, and between episodes we need the channel artwork done properly. We are NOT reshooting and we do not need the video re-edited here. What we're handing you: three raw episode recordings (episodes 07, 08, and 09 of this season), our channel logo, and a hand-built InDesign episode-card template plus the episode roster.

Here's the problem and the job. The three episodes were shot on three different nights and the studio lighting was different every time, so a still lifted from each one looks like it belongs to a different show — none of them match out of camera. We clipped a neutral 18% grey card to the desk mic-flag in every episode so you have an honest reference to balance against. (1) Pull one strong representative frame from each episode and bring all three to ONE consistent DAYDRIFT channel look: use the grey card each frame carries to neutralize it and land all three on one shared white point and one brightness, so a viewer scrolling our uploads can't tell which night each was shot. Judge each frame on its own — they start from different places, so the same correction won't be right for all three, and don't over-process a frame that already reads true to its card just to chase a number; a look that's already right shouldn't be stripped. Tell us, per frame, the white-balance and exposure you landed on so we can confirm the set is matched and not eyeballed. (2) On the hero (episode 07), our coral neon sign that spells DAYDRIFT behind the hosts photographs a little pink after you neutralize the frame — deepen just the neon to our true brand coral, a rich in-family deepen that keeps the tube glow and the spill on the desk natural; do not tint the whole frame and do not touch skin or the set. (3) Reframe each graded frame into a 16:9 YouTube thumbnail with the hosts pushed to one side so there's clean space for our episode title, grey card cropped out of the finished thumbnail. (4) Our logo only exists as a phone photo taken on a cluttered studio desk and it sits a touch crooked — lift it cleanly off that background, straighten and sharpen it, and give us both a clean transparent PNG and a razor-sharp vector so it prints crisp on the card masthead. (5) Finally build the episode cards: we've hand-built the InDesign single-record card template with the real placeholder fields and an image slot, and we're giving you the roster — merge them so every episode gets its own one-page card with its number, title, guest, air date and runtime set from the roster verbatim and its matching graded frame dropped in, then hand back a press-ready ~300 DPI PDF with one card per episode and episode 07 leading the set for the sponsor kit. Keep it light-hearted and consistent — one channel, three episodes, never stiff.

inputs.name: episode_07_overthinkers_raw.mp4
inputs.gen_prompt: Raw 1080p podcast recording, two casual hosts seated at a wooden desk with matte-black microphones on boom arms, relaxed two-shot framing, they chat and laugh with small natural gestures. Behind them a coral-pink illuminated neon sign spelling a short show name glows softly on the wall. The studio is lit by COOL daylight-balanced LED panels giving a distinct blue-cyan cast, and the frame is slightly underexposed and a little flat as if straight off the camera. A neutral 18% grey reference card is clipped to the desk mic-flag at the lower-left, clearly visible and uncropped. Everything is plain and unbranded except the fictional neon show name; matte-black mics carry no logos. Realistic candid studio look, no CGI gloss, no on-screen text overlays.
inputs.realism_notes: HERO episode. Short representative clip stand-in for the full episode 07 master (~1080p). Provides a real frame for video_render_frame and cuttable footage for the trailer Quick Cut. Cool/blue cast + slight underexposure = a genuine warm-the-WB + lift correction. The in-frame 18% grey card is the free checkable neutral target. The coral neon sign is the masked-recolor subject: after the frame is neutralized the coral reads a touch pink and must be deepened to true brand coral within its own hue family. NO real brand/logo — the neon spells the fictional show name only.

inputs.name: episode_08_midnight_snack_raw.mp4
inputs.gen_prompt: Raw 1080p podcast recording, the same two hosts at the same wooden desk with matte-black mics, different night: the room is lit only by WARM tungsten practical lamps for a cozy late-night vibe, giving a strong orange cast, and the exposure is a touch BRIGHT. Natural conversational two-shot, gentle laughter and small gestures. A neutral 18% grey reference card is clipped to the desk mic-flag at the lower-right, clearly visible and uncropped. Plain unbranded set, matte-black mics with no text or logos. Realistic candid studio look, no CGI, no on-screen text.
inputs.realism_notes: Short representative clip stand-in for the full episode 08 master (~1080p). Warm/orange cast + slightly bright = the OPPOSITE correction to episode 07 (cool the WB, pull exposure down) toward the SAME shared white point — the trap is copying episode 07's numbers. Grey card in frame is the neutralization target; different desk corner so the crop that removes it differs from the hero's.

inputs.name: episode_09_unsolicited_advice_raw.mp4
inputs.gen_prompt: Raw 1080p podcast recording, one host solo at the same wooden desk with a matte-black mic, shot under properly bi-color-balanced LED light so the scene is neutrally exposed and correctly white-balanced; the set features warm walnut wall paneling and a soft amber accent glow that are an intentional cozy aesthetic, not a lighting error. Calm natural single-shot, small gestures. A neutral 18% grey reference card is clipped to the desk mic-flag at the lower-left, clearly visible and uncropped, and it reads a clean neutral grey. Plain unbranded set, matte-black mic with no text or logos. Realistic candid studio look, no CGI, no on-screen text.
inputs.realism_notes: THE TRAP episode. Short representative clip stand-in for the full episode 09 master (~1080p). Shot under neutral, correctly-balanced light so its in-frame grey card ALREADY reads neutral — the warm walnut/amber look is the real, intended set, not a cast. The correct move is essentially NO white-balance shift (only match brightness to the shared target). A naive agent that batch-applies 'warm the cool / cool the warm' or 'cools an imagined warm cast' pushes the card off-neutral and strips the intended channel warmth. Decision must be driven by THIS card, not the batch.

inputs.name: daydrift_logo_photographed.png
inputs.gen_prompt: A phone photo of the DAYDRIFT channel logo lockup — a bold friendly rounded-sans wordmark reading 'DAYDRIFT' in deep navy with a small coral paper-boat/drift glyph to the left — printed on a card and lying on a CLUTTERED studio desk (coffee mug, tangled cable, sticky notes, a pair of headphones) so the mark must be separated from busy surroundings. The card sits slightly rotated about 3 degrees and off-center, shot under even light, the wordmark crisp and legible with flat navy-and-coral color. High resolution, roughly 4000 px on the long edge as if from a modern phone camera.
inputs.realism_notes: The channel logo as it realistically exists — a phone photo on a busy desk, not a clean vector file. Busy background => a real remove_background isolation job (not a luminance threshold). Slight rotation => a real auto_straighten job before tracing. Flat two-color legible mark => once isolated, straightened, crisped and cropped to bounds it vectorizes to a clean SVG. Declared at ~4000 px long edge (camera scale) so isolation, crop-to-bounds and vectorize have real resolution and nothing is upscaled. 'DAYDRIFT' is an invented, IP-clean mark; gemini-3-pro-image chosen because the mark carries legible type.

inputs.name: daydrift_episode_card.indd
inputs.gen_prompt: AUTHORED DELIVERABLE (cannot be model-generated): a genuine, hand-built Adobe InDesign document (.indd/.idml) for a SINGLE-RECORD episode card — ONE episode per page, US Letter (8.5x11) landscape for the sponsor/press kit. It must contain live InDesign data-merge placeholder fields <<episode_number>>, <<episode_title>>, <<guest>>, <<air_date>>, <<runtime>>, a masthead image frame wired to an @-prefixed @logo image-path merge column so the merge drops the vectorized channel wordmark into the masthead, and ONE 16:9 image frame (about 4.8 in wide) wired to a second @-prefixed @thumb image-path merge column so the merge drops the matching graded episode frame into the card — TWO @image-path columns in all (@logo masthead + @thumb photo). Built by hand in InDesign so the merge fields AND both image frames actually bind. Explicitly NOT a convert_pdf_to_indd output and NOT a multi-record grid: document_merge_data_layout emits one file per row, so the template holds exactly one record's worth of fields.
inputs.realism_notes: document_merge_data_layout REQUIRES a user-authored .indd carrying real <<fields>> plus genuine @image-path columns, and it produces ONE FILE PER ROW — so a single-record episode card is the correct, connector-doable shape. TWO image columns (@logo, @thumb) mean the agent-produced vector wordmark reaches the masthead ONLY via the @logo merge column (never free-placed at coordinates) exactly as the graded frame reaches the photo frame via @thumb. The ~4.8 in image frame keeps a 16:9 graded frame delivered at ~1600-1760 px well above 300 DPI at trim. Supplied as an input, not a chain output; a PDF-converted .indd or a multi-up grid would not bind / cannot be produced.

inputs.name: daydrift_episode_roster.csv
inputs.gen_prompt: Generate a CSV with columns episode_number,episode_title,guest,air_date,runtime,@thumb,@logo holding exactly THREE rows, one per episode: (07, 'The Overthinkers Club', 'Marisol Vane', 'Air date Fri Sep 12', '48 min', @ep07_card_img.jpg, @daydrift_logo_vector.svg); (08, 'Midnight Snack Debates', 'Theo Kessler', 'Air date Fri Sep 19', '52 min', @ep08_card_img.jpg, @daydrift_logo_vector.svg); (09, 'Unsolicited Advice', 'Solo episode', 'Air date Fri Sep 26', '41 min', @ep09_card_img.jpg, @daydrift_logo_vector.svg). Column names must exactly match the template merge fields <<episode_number>>,<<episode_title>>,<<guest>>,<<air_date>>,<<runtime>>; the @thumb image-path column resolves to the agent's produced graded card frames (one per episode) and the @logo image-path column resolves to the agent's produced vector wordmark (the SAME daydrift_logo_vector.svg on every row, since the masthead art is constant across the set).
inputs.realism_notes: Three rows => the one-file-per-row merge must produce exactly three finished cards (page-count = row-count = 3 is the acceptance gate). Guest names ('Marisol Vane', 'Theo Kessler') and titles are invented and IP-clean. TWO @image columns are the binding contract: @thumb points at each episode's own produced card frame and @logo points at the produced vector wordmark, so document_merge_data_layout drops the correct graded frame into the photo frame AND the vectorized masthead art into the masthead frame — the ONLY connector-legal way an agent-produced mark reaches the laid-out page (no free-form placement at coordinates). @logo carries the same wordmark filename on all three rows because the masthead is identical across episodes. Text-only document_merge_data_vector is explicitly the WRONG tool because it cannot bind either image column.

outputs.name: graded_masters_cardbearing_x3
outputs.spec: Three RETAINED full-frame neutralized masters (native ~1920x1080), one per episode, each with its in-frame 18% grey card STILL PRESENT and uncropped — the hero (ep 07) additionally carrying the deepened coral neon. Each frame is neutralized BY EYE to its own grey card and all three are brought to ONE shared channel white point and brightness. These retained card-bearing masters are the reference the thumbnail and card-frame crops are derived from, and are the files the grader measures for grey-card neutrality (per-channel R,G,B spread within a tight tolerance) and cross-frame white-point/brightness match — neutrality is graded HERE, never on a file the card is cropped from. Accompanied by the per-frame applied-parameter report (white-balance temperature/tint and exposure the agent dialed). Adjust/downscale of the native 1080p frames only, never upscaled.

outputs.name: youtube_thumbnails_x3
outputs.spec: Three 1280x720 (16:9) YouTube episode thumbnails, one per episode, each a card-cropped reframe of that episode's graded master with the hosts pushed to one side leaving clean title negative space; on the hero (ep 07) the coral neon deepened to the true brand coral within its own hue band with the tube glow intact. Because these crops derive from the matched masters they carry the one shared white point and brightness; the grey card is deliberately cropped OUT, so this deliverable is graded for card-EXCLUSION (no grey card anywhere in frame) and shared look — the neutrality tolerance is checked on graded_masters_cardbearing_x3, NOT on this cropped file. Downscale from the native 1080p master only, never upscaled.

outputs.name: ep_card_frames_x3
outputs.spec: Three full-resolution 16:9 card-cropped frames (~1600-1760 px long edge) derived from the matched graded masters, grey card cropped OUT (this deliverable is checked for card-EXCLUSION here, not for card neutrality — neutrality lives on graded_masters_cardbearing_x3), one per episode, that bind into the episode-card image frame via the roster @thumb column at >=300 DPI at the card trim.

outputs.name: daydrift_logo_clean.png
outputs.spec: The DAYDRIFT logo lifted off its cluttered desk background to a clean transparent PNG, straightened, sharpened and color-true (navy wordmark + coral glyph), cropped to the tight bounds of the mark — the 'PNG/transparent' graphic-asset deliverable.

outputs.name: daydrift_logo_vector.svg
outputs.spec: Infinitely-scalable vector SVG of the cleaned logo, traced only AFTER the photo is isolated, straightened, crisped and cropped to bounds — razor-sharp at masthead scale with no captured desk clutter or skew. The 'vector format' graphic-asset deliverable and the card masthead art.

outputs.name: DAYDRIFT_EpisodeCards_perEpisode_x3.pdf
outputs.spec: Exactly three press-ready US Letter (8.5x11) landscape episode cards — ONE single-record card per roster row (page-count = row-count = 3) — exported from the one-file-per-row InDesign data-merge; each card binds its episode_number/episode_title/guest/air_date/runtime verbatim from the roster with its matching graded 16:9 frame dropped into the image frame via the @thumb column and the vector wordmark bound into the masthead frame via the @logo column; ~300 DPI print quality.

outputs.name: daydrift_trailer_coldopen.mp4
outputs.spec: A short (~12s) engagement-based highlight cut of the SINGLE hero episode 07 master clip via Quick Cut (the AI selects the moments; NOT a frame-accurate timestamp trim and NOT an assembly of multiple clips), output duration shorter than the source clip, 1920x1080, for the channel's cold-open teaser.

connector_workflow.inputs_from: episode_07_overthinkers_raw.mp4, episode_08_midnight_snack_raw.mp4, episode_09_unsolicited_advice_raw.mp4, daydrift_logo_photographed.png, daydrift_episode_card.indd, daydrift_episode_roster.csv
connector_workflow.note: Load the three raw episode clips, the photographed logo, the authored episode-card .indd and the roster CSV into the working project in one batch so every downstream step has real asset references. Single upload — plumbing, not counted as difficulty.

Pull one strong representative two-shot still from episode 07 (hosts framed, coral neon sign and the desk grey card both in frame) to build the hero thumbnail from. Frame extraction only — no generation.
Pull one representative still from episode 08 (two-shot with the grey card visible). Frame extraction only.
Pull one representative still from episode 09 (solo host, grey card visible). Frame extraction only.

HERO grade + establish the channel target. Episode 07 ran COOL/blue and slightly underexposed, so WARM the temperature and nudge tint until the in-frame 18% grey card reads truly neutral (R=G=B), then LIFT exposure and set contrast so the card sits at mid-grey and the frame reaches the shared brightness. This reported white-balance/exposure IS the common target the other two must hit. Reason it to THIS card; do not reuse another frame's numbers. Authored from primitives (temperature/tint/exposure/contrast/highlights/shadows), NOT a preset and NOT auto-tone. Report the move.

On the neutralized hero, semantically select ONLY the illuminated coral neon sign spelling the show name behind the hosts ('the glowing coral neon sign on the wall'). Isolates the recolor to that object so skin, mics and the set are untouched. Returns a maskURI — a real object selection, not a hue or coordinate pick.

Masked recolor pass 1 (consumes hero + neon mask): the neon reads a touch pink after neutralization, so keep it in the coral/red-orange family but deepen it — a SMALL within-band hue nudge (well under ~60 deg, staying in coral, NOT a near-complementary rotation) toward the true brand coral, letting the tube's existing luminosity carry the glow. image_adjust_hsl is the ONLY masked recolor path; image_apply_color_overlay is whole-image (would tint the hosts and set) and image_fill_area is a flat solid fill (would kill the neon glow) — both are wrong here.

Masked recolor pass 2 (same mask): settle the coral-band saturation and luminance so the neon lands on the rich brand coral instead of a hot pink or a dull brick, still riding the original luminosity so the tube glow and the coral spill on the desk stay natural. A deepen-and-settle in the same hue family — not a swing to a new hue. ep07_graded is the finished full-res hero frame WITH the grey card still in frame — it is RETAINED as the hero's card-bearing neutralized master (graded_masters_cardbearing_x3), the file the grader checks for grey-card neutrality; the card-cropped card frame (9) and thumbnail (10) are derived from it and never carry the card.

Clean 16:9 reframe of the graded hero that crops the lower-left grey card OUT of frame while keeping the hosts and neon, downscaled to ~1760x990 for the card image frame. onSubjectClipping='extract', downscale/reframe of existing pixels only — never canvas-extend, never upscale. Feeds the episode-card @thumb cell for row 07.

YouTube thumbnail reframe of the graded hero: push the hosts to one side leaving clean title negative space on the other, grey card cropped out, downscaled to exactly 1280x720. Downscale-only from the 1080p frame. DELIVERABLE (youtube_thumbnails_x3, hero).

Episode 08 grade to the SAME target set in step 5, reasoned to THIS card. It ran WARM/orange and slightly bright, so this frame moves the OPPOSITE direction from the hero: COOL the temperature (negative) and adjust tint until its grey card reads neutral at the shared white point, and PULL exposure DOWN to the shared brightness. Copying the hero's warming/lifting numbers here is exactly the trap that breaks the match. Report the (distinct) move. ep08_neutral keeps its grey card in frame and is RETAINED as episode 08's card-bearing neutralized master (graded_masters_cardbearing_x3) — the file the grader checks for neutrality; the card-cropped frame (12) and thumbnail (13) derive from it.

Clean 16:9 reframe cropping the lower-RIGHT grey card out (different corner than the hero), downscaled to ~1760x990 for the card image frame. onSubjectClipping='extract', downscale-only. Feeds the @thumb cell for row 08.
YouTube thumbnail reframe of the graded episode-08 frame with title negative space, grey card cropped out, downscaled to exactly 1280x720. Downscale-only. DELIVERABLE (youtube_thumbnails_x3).

THE TRAP FRAME. Episode 09 was shot under correctly-balanced light, so its in-frame grey card ALREADY reads neutral and the warm walnut/amber set is the intended look, not a cast. The correct move is essentially NO white-balance shift — hold WB and only match brightness/exposure to the shared target from step 5. A naive agent that batch-applies the cool-frame 'warm it' or the warm-frame 'cool it' correction, or 'cools an imagined warm cast', will neutralize the card off-neutral and strip the intended channel warmth. Decision driven by THIS card, not the batch. Report that WB was held (only exposure matched). ep09_neutral keeps its grey card in frame and is RETAINED as episode 09's card-bearing neutralized master (graded_masters_cardbearing_x3) — the file the grader checks for neutrality (and here confirms the card stayed neutral because WB was correctly held); the card-cropped frame (15) and thumbnail (16) derive from it.
Clean 16:9 reframe cropping the grey card out, downscaled to ~1760x990 for the card image frame. onSubjectClipping='extract', downscale-only. Feeds the @thumb cell for row 09.

YouTube thumbnail reframe of the graded episode-09 frame with title negative space, grey card cropped out, downscaled to exactly 1280x720. Downscale-only. DELIVERABLE (youtube_thumbnails_x3). The three thumbnails now share one white point, each neutralized to its own grey card.

Prep-before-trace step 1: lift the DAYDRIFT mark off its cluttered studio-desk background to transparency (isolates the wordmark + glyph from the mug/cable/notes clutter). remove_background -> transparency, the CORRECT path — NOT select_subject -> invert_selection -> image_fill_area, which would solid-fill and destroy the counters inside the letterforms.
Prep-before-trace step 2: the photographed card sat ~3 deg rotated, so level the isolated mark before tracing — feeding a skewed raster to vectorize would bake the rotation into the vector edges.

Prep-before-trace step 3: push contrast/clarity so the navy wordmark and coral glyph separate hard and read as flat, true brand color — a soft phone-photo raster traces into ragged, doubled edges. Authored crisp pass, no color reinvention beyond locking the flat navy/coral.

Prep-before-trace step 4: crop away the now-transparent surround to the tight bounds of the mark so the trace captures only the wordmark + glyph, not empty canvas. This trimmed transparent PNG is the clean-PNG DELIVERABLE and the input to vectorize.

Trace the prepared raster (isolated, straightened, crisped, cropped to bounds, transparent) into a clean SVG for the card masthead and channel use. Tracing the raw desk photo instead would produce a skewed, clutter-bounded, fuzzy silhouette — the trap this prep chain avoids. DELIVERABLE (vector).

Initialize an upload session for the three full-res graded card frames plus the vector wordmark, uploaded under the exact names the roster references, so the merge can resolve them by the roster @thumb column (per-episode frames) and the @logo column (the masthead wordmark).
Finalize the upload; returns the asset URNs the roster's @thumb column resolves to for each episode's single-record card and the URN the @logo column resolves to for the masthead wordmark.

One-file-per-row InDesign data-merge: bind each of the three roster rows (episode_number/episode_title/guest/air_date/runtime) into the authored SINGLE-RECORD .indd's live <<fields>>, drop that row's graded 16:9 frame into the @thumb image frame AND the agent's vectorized wordmark into the @logo masthead frame — producing EXACTLY ONE merged card per row (three cards). The vector wordmark reaches the layout ONLY through the @logo merge column (an agent-produced mark can never be free-placed at coordinates). [T] requires the hand-authored template. document_merge_data_vector is the WRONG tool (text-only, cannot bind @thumb or @logo) and a convert_pdf_to_indd template would not bind — both avoided.

Export the merged single-record cards to a press-ready ~300 DPI US Letter landscape PDF, one card per episode. Because the roster orders episode 07 first, page 1 of this merged PDF IS the hero card — no separate single-record export is needed or possible (document_render_layout exports the WHOLE merged multi-page document, not one named record). Acceptance: page-count = row-count = 3; if fewer, the merge collapsed rows and failed. Each placed frame renders >=300 DPI at the ~4.8 in image frame. DELIVERABLE (pdf).

AI engagement-based highlight cut of the SINGLE hero episode 07 master clip for the ~12s cold-open teaser (the AI selects the moments — this is NOT a frame-accurate timestamp trim, which the connector cannot do). video_create_quick_cut only SHORTENS one supplied clip: one source in, output duration < source, no assembly of multiple clips and no lengthening. 1920x1080. DELIVERABLE (video).

chaining_note: Strict output-to-input chaining across three tributaries that converge on the episode-card merge. VIDEO->FRAME tributary: one batch upload (1) fans into three video_render_frame pulls (2/3/4), one representative still per episode. Each still runs its own grade sub-chain that reasons a DIFFERENT correction to ONE shared target: episode 07 (hero) neutralizes cool->warm + lift (5, establishing the channel target), then a two-pass masked recolor deepens the coral neon within its own hue band (select_by_prompt 6 -> masked image_adjust_hsl 7 -> masked image_adjust_hsl 8, both consuming ep07_neon_mask), then a clean card-frame reframe removing the grey card (9) and a 1280x720 thumbnail reframe with title space (10); episode 08 neutralizes the OPPOSITE way warm->cool + pull-down (11) then reframes to card frame (12) and thumbnail (13); episode 09 is the TRAP, WB held and only brightness matched (14), then card frame (15) and thumbnail (16). LOGO tributary is a genuine prep-before-trace chain: remove_background off the cluttered desk (17) -> auto_straighten the ~3 deg skew (18) -> crisp adjustments (19) -> crop_to_bounds = daydrift_logo_clean.png (20) -> vectorize = daydrift_logo_vector.svg (21). MERGE convergence: the three full-res card frames + the vector wordmark upload (22) -> finalize (23) -> document_merge_data_layout (24) also consuming the authored single-record .indd and the roster CSV, resolving BOTH image columns per row (@thumb -> that episode's graded frame, @logo -> the vectorized wordmark), emitting one merged card per row -> a single export of the WHOLE merged set to the per-episode PDF (25), whose first page is the hero card because episode 07 leads the roster (no per-record named export). A parallel Quick Cut (26) shortens the single hero episode 07 clip into the cold-open teaser (one source in, output shorter than source — no multi-clip assembly). Every post-upload step consumes a named prior output; the merge converges all three frame chains plus the logo and roster, the agent-produced wordmark reaching the masthead ONLY via the @logo merge column. 26 calls, 15 distinct Adobe tools.
difficulty_rationale: Long-horizon flagship with difficulty from DEPTH, not plumbing: 26 connector calls, 15 distinct Adobe tools across three groups (video [A] frame-pull + Quick Cut, image [C] grade/mask/recolor/vectorize, asset [C] storage, document [T]/[C] merge/export) — above the >=10 call / >=6 distinct-tool floor even after stripping the single upload and the two merge-upload plumbing steps. The core is NOT a repeated recipe: the three frame grades are three DIFFERENT reasoned decisions forced to converge on one measurable target (the in-frame 18% grey card): the cool hero warmed and lifted, the warm episode cooled and pulled down, and the trap episode's white balance HELD because its card is already neutral and its warmth is intentional — so a blanket batch correction cannot pass, and 'cooling an imagined cast' on the trap frame is a visible fail. Layered on top are a masked, luminosity-preserving neon recolor executed as two within-family image_adjust_hsl passes (a coral deepen-and-settle, an in-band adjacent shift the tool can actually hold — NOT a near-complementary rotation — with a written rationale for why color_overlay and fill_area are both wrong), a genuine prep-before-trace vectorize of a cluttered, skewed phone photo (isolate->straighten->crisp->crop-to-bounds->trace), and a one-file-per-row data-merge into a hand-authored single-record template that is the owned composed endpoint. Respects every hard limit: no generative fill/expand, no compositing of graphics into the video, no text-to-image, no upscaling, no timestamp trim (Quick Cut is engagement-based), no per-artboard export; convert_pdf_to_indd is NOT used; image_crop_and_resize is downscale-only with onSubjectClipping='extract'; and no deprecated tool names appear (all tone/WB via image_apply_adjustments).
hardness_rationale: FAILURE GATE (a wrong DECISION, not a self-measurement): each pulled frame carries a physical 18% grey card and, because the card is cropped out of the delivered thumbnails and card frames, each neutralized frame is RETAINED as a card-bearing master (graded_masters_cardbearing_x3, card still in frame); the acceptance criterion is that every retained master's grey card reads a clean neutral (per-channel R,G,B spread within a tight tolerance) with all three matched to ONE white point and brightness, and the delivered card-cropped thumbnails/frames are checked separately for card-EXCLUSION only — neutrality is never graded on a file the card is cropped from. The agent must REPORT the per-frame white-balance and exposure it applied (by eye, never a read pixel value), so an eyeballed or uniform correction is caught. The trap frame (episode 09) is the sharpest trip: its card is already neutral, so the correct decision is to HOLD white balance, and any batch 'warm it / cool it' move visibly strips the intended channel warmth. A second checkable gate sits in the merge: output page-count must equal roster row-count = 3 (document_merge_data_layout is one-file-per-row). HUMAN-HARD ELEMENTS: (1) cross-asset tonal consistency to a measurable target across three frames pulled from three differently-lit episodes, which demands the counter-intuitive insight that a matched OUTPUT needs DIFFERENT per-frame corrections in opposite directions reasoned from each frame's own card; (2) prep-before-trace discipline plus the correct isolation path on a cluttered, skewed phone photo of the logo (remove_background -> straighten -> crisp -> crop-to-bounds -> vectorize, NOT tracing the raw photo and NOT select->invert->fill); (3) a masked, luminosity-preserving within-family neon recolor via the only masked recolor path (image_adjust_hsl), not whole-image color_overlay or flat fill_area; (4) placing BOTH the graded frame and the agent-vectorized wordmark into a laid-out page only via genuine @-image-column bindings (@thumb, @logo) in an authored .indd merge — never free-placing a mark at coordinates. TRAP: applying one white-balance/exposure correction to all three frames (the two-session cast split guarantees it will not match), and specifically 'correcting' the trap episode whose warmth is real; a second trap is tracing the raw logo photo (skew + desk clutter baked into the vector). MEASURABLE ACCEPTANCE: grey card neutral within tolerance on the three RETAINED card-bearing masters at one shared white point + reported per-frame WB/exposure params, with the card-cropped thumbnails/card frames checked separately for card-exclusion; neon recolor confined to its mask (coral deepened in-family, glow intact); logo a clean skew-free transparent-ground SVG; thumbnails exactly 1280x720 downscaled from 1080p; exactly one press-ready ~300 DPI US Letter card per roster row (page-count = row-count = 3, episode 07 leading, no per-record named export) with each frame placed >=300 DPI at trim.
